predeclaredReading.betterIs: The guarded arm is read as better only if it passes STRICTLY MORE than 21 of the 30 predeclared tasks (the reference's count in the immediately preceding window). A tie is not a gain and a loss is a loss; the reference is never re-measured to manufacture a fairer comparison.
predeclaredReading.whyStrict: The two 2026-10-05 arms both carried a real verdict in all 30 cells, so the completion tie-break cannot decide anything: only the pass count and the per-cell flips can.
predeclaredReading.completion: Completion is read per arm as cells with a real graded verdict versus cells left without one (error / not-evaluated / pre-model environment failure / provider transport failure); a verdict-less cell is a binding failure, never a capability loss.
predeclaredReading.score: Score is not used as a bar. The 2026-10-05 manifest's literal 'passed + datacurve partial' reading proved uninformative (the partial is dominated by 66,265 pass-to-pass tests, so a failed datacurve cell still contributes ≈1.0); the discriminating readings are the pass count and the datacurve fail-to-pass fraction, both reported.
predeclaredReading.delivery: On the two graded read-back cells (/app/recovered.json, /app/out.txt) presence and first-write time are read exactly as before. This is the mechanism the clause exists for; neither arm delivered in the previous window, so a delivery here is a mechanism observation, and a pass requires the cell's own verifier.
predeclaredReading.flips: Every cell whose verdict differs from the reference's is listed, with the specification-gap tasks marked and an explicit exclusion count so a reader can see the reading with and without them.
predeclaredReading.cost: Any cell whose disposition or failing set regresses against the reference is recorded as cost even if the count moves forward.
predeclaredReading.censoring: A cell bounded by its budget or a declared stop is a right-censored observation reported with its span: never excluded, never counted as a gain.
predeclaredReading.uncertainty: One attempt per cell; the guarded arm runs in a later window than the reference, so the comparison carries window difference (provider load, runner capacity, time of day) exactly as the previous contrast did in the opposite direction. A within-window or cross-window flip is a diagnostic observation, never an effect size.

fairnessDisclosures: No user prefix, no task-specific hint, no grader output and no evaluator feedback reaches the arm; the only text delta against main is the two clauses, and against 2.18.0 it is the rewritten landing line.
The added text names no task, file, value, tool alias, evaluator or grader; it is ASCII-only and states generic discipline (verified by token scan on the shipped text).
One attempt per cell; no best-of-N, no retry-until-pass, no cell exclusion, no latency threshold, no cell dropped for being slow.
The reference arm is NOT re-dispatched: its number comes from its own previous-window run, and that window difference is disclosed rather than hidden.
Task environments are internet-connected as frozen (no closed-book claim); any cell with an upstream-fetch signature is recorded, never credited as a delivery or pass mechanism.
The arm refs are never moved after dispatch; nothing is merged by this study, and no pass@1 for the 2026-10-05 window is reinterpreted.
readingPlan: Bind the arm: run headSha equals the guarded ref commit; every cell's first-request Skill instruction is 6,642 bytes with SHA-256 0c588320…; every record agrees on one candidate id; candidate.single / provider.single / instructions.frozen intact, provider.reasoningEffort=max, coverage.full passed.

Tabulate per cell: disposition, reward, f2p/p2p, terminal cause, duration against budget, call count, max call span, deliverable presence on the two graded paths with first-write time, upstream-fetch signature.
Read the pass count against the predeclared bar (strictly more than 21), then the 26-cell subset against the reference's same 26 cells, then the flips with and without the specification-gap tasks.
Write the outcome into this file's outcome section, commit and push to codex/prompt-preservation-execution.
Never flip or merge PR #212 on this reading alone: the PR's own gate also requires an independent review of the 2.19.0 diff.

The smoke gate is already satisfied: the same profile and build path produced two green 30-task runs on 2026-10-05, and the only change is one instruction line.

notes: This study exists because the 2026-10-05 contrast found the unconditional landing clause costly on source-change tasks (datacurve 1 vs 5, fail-to-pass 0.8560 vs 0.9773) and because 2.18.0 carried no anti-fabrication guard.
The measured text is frozen at 348746e6 for clean attribution: against main the delta is exactly the preservation sentence plus the rewritten landing line; no further prompt edit enters this run.

2.19.0's rewritten landing line reads: land the answer the moment reasoning supports it, scoped to what the task reads back (a value or a produced output file), never through a script that has not been run and before any further verification, with the explicit guards that landing early never licenses a guess or placeholder and never licenses finalizing a source change before its verification.

Seven cells flipped: three to the guarded arm (one of them an overlap cell that had never passed at this profile) and four to the reference, for a net of minus one.

reviewRecord.headline: Text, architecture boundary, fairness/hardcoding and the existing pins all hold and the text does not need to be withdrawn; but the verdict was not an unconditional ACCEPT — it listed a minimal fix set and stated that a reading of 21 or fewer is a REJECT regardless.
openFixes: F1 (high, merge-readiness): the PR description/title still describe 2.18.0 and do not record this 20-vs-21 reading or the earlier 18-vs-21 one.

F3 (medium): the 2.19.0 commit message asserts a causal claim ("i.e. the landing clause pushed source-change work into a write-first pattern") where every other record hedges it as plausible and explicitly not an effect size.
F4 (medium): spec 306 does not record the Product enumeration delta having been accepted first, which the admission rules require and the 303 precedent records verbatim.

F5 (medium-low, text-neutral): the landing clause itself carries no byte identity — both hashes are taken after removing it, so an equal-length rewrite of that clause plus the test literal passes every assertion (reproduced). Pin the full-text or clause sha256.
F2/F6/F7 (low): claim-versus-text wording (the clause's head is unconditional while the enumeration claims it is scoped), 306's delta counting, and one inherited unbacked enumeration half-sentence.
reviewRecord.note: None of these fixes was applied in this run: the reading failed, and the standing rule is that a failed reading ends the attempt without further edits.

decision.merge: NOT merged. PR Simon-He95/best-agent#212 stays Draft, head 348746e6…, MERGEABLE, untouched by this readout.
failingConditions: (a) The benefit condition: 20 passes against the required strictly-more-than-21. A one-cell loss is a loss.

(b) The independent review's own decision rule: its verdict was a conditional accept whose stated rule is that a reading of 21 or fewer is a REJECT regardless; its five-item fix list is also still open.
decision.conditionThatHolds: (c) No hardcoded or task-specific text: the shipped 2.19.0 text names no task, file, value, tool alias, evaluator or grader, and the pinned negative loop for the six forbidden host-mechanism names passes.
decision.nothingDone: No `gh pr ready`, no `gh pr merge`, no branch or ref change, no arm ref moved, nothing merged anywhere.
decision.whatWouldChangeTheReading: A new predeclared cohort in which the shipped text passes strictly more than 21 of the 30 tasks, with the same binding discipline and the graded-delivery cells actually delivering. Because a one-cell gap on this corpus has already flipped across windows with no prompt change, a repeat of the same contrast would be the honest way to tell a stable gap from run variance.
alternativePathsRecorded: The review's text-neutral fixes (F1/F3/F4/F5 and the F2/F6/F7 wording) remain available for any future attempt; they do not change the measured text.

The guarded clause's mechanism now has one supporting observation at this profile (db-wal delivered at 138.6 s and passed) and one still-unsolved cell (gcode never delivered by any arm). The CLI-side reserved-boundary work is tracked as best-agent issue #213.
